comparison: Perfect agreement on imaging technology (C3, C19, C20, C112-C115). Both evaluations find the technical innovation well-supported. Peer reviewers praised it as 'very sophisticated' and 'powerful,' matching OpenEval's assessment of comprehensive technical specifications.

Perfect agreement on stick insect literature context (C104-C107). Both evaluations accept these as valid established findings from prior work that provide appropriate baseline for comparison with fly results.

Strong agreement on gait pattern findings (C56-C67). Both accept gradual rather than discrete gait transitions and the quantification of noncanonical gaits. Peer reviewers found the data 'fairly convincing' that tripod gait occurs at all speeds with diminishing frequency in slower flies.

Strong agreement on sensory-deprived phenotypes (C4-C5, C23-C25, C84-C90). Both find the key result well-supported: coordination maintained despite precision defects. Peer reviewers called this 'the most interesting aspect' and 'a surprising result,' accepting the validity of the findings.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding distinct neural programs (C22, C75-C76, C93). OpenEval notes these claims are speculative without direct neural evidence. Peer reviewers questioned the rationale for three speed groups and requested statistical verification of the 20 mm/s break point.

Disagreement on CPG communication mechanisms (C95-C96, C98). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting strong mechanistic claims lack direct circuit evidence. Peer reviewers SUPPORTED the interpretation, accepting that flies differ from stick insects in CPG-based coordination, though they acknowledged the speculation.

Disagreement on speed-dependent sensory feedback interpretation (C94, C100). OpenEval finds mechanistic claims about CPG communication speculative. Peer reviewers explicitly accepted the interpretation that 'flies may be less dependent on sensory feedback when they walk fast.'

Disagreement on speed distribution characterization (C28-C29, C117-C118). OpenEval finds the statistical treatment appropriate, noting acknowledgment of non-Gaussian outliers. Peer reviewers questioned how outliers were determined and whether they should be excluded, indicating uncertainty.

Disagreement on spatial precision parameters (C41-C48). OpenEval finds these well-supported with clear methodology and statistics. Peer reviewers expressed 'significant concerns' about statistical methods, recommending ANOVA instead of t-tests and Mann-Whitney U-tests used.

Disagreement on kinematic parameters (C30-C37). OpenEval finds these adequately supported with appropriate sample size and statistical analyses. Peer reviewers questioned the statistical methods as 'not adequate,' affecting confidence in speed-dependent comparisons.

Disagreement on phase relationship findings (C78-C79). OpenEval finds circular statistics appropriate and conclusions supported. Peer reviewers' general statistical concerns about methods apply to these phase analyses as well.

Disagreement on CPG background characterization (C1, C8-C10). OpenEval accepts these as appropriately cited established knowledge. Peer reviewers found the Introduction presents 'a naïve view of how CPGs work' and requested reworking to reflect a 'more sophisticated view.'

Partial overlap on leg alignment observations (C72-C73). OpenEval finds these observations well-supported. Peer reviewers' statistical methodology concerns apply to these speed-dependent findings, creating uncertainty about the analyses.

Minimal overlap on leg positioning (C49). OpenEval supports the positional observations while noting functional interpretations are speculative. Peer reviewers' statistical concerns affect confidence in these observations as well.
OpenEval found leg-specific analyses (C38-C40) appropriately supported with reasonable inference about hypotheses from prior stick insect work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval found instantaneous speed variation observations (C52-C55) well-supported by high temporal resolution imaging. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rated speculative interpretations about sensory feedback on complex terrain (C101) and motor neuron recruitment (C111) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable hypotheses lacking experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval found method applicability and limitation claims (C102-C103) appropriately supported and scoped. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
